catalog_quote: 1.4.6 Stress. Primary word stress is on the initial syllable: /wérne/ 'food'; /thápuji/ 'friend'; /kúdithur/ 'will see'. Primary phrase stress is on the last word of the phrase: /kìin wérne/ 'that food'; /ngìthun thápuji/ 'my friend'; /ngàta nìwenthar kúrithur/ 'I'll see him'. There are exceptions to this, namely a set of nominal expressions with /tangka/ 'man' as the head noun, and with a demonstrative of or other modifier preceding the head noun. In these expressions, the noun encliticizes to [p. 30] the modifier, and then undergoes truncation, thus appearing as /-rta/, or is assimilated to a preceding apico-alveolar, as /-ta/. For example, there exist the expressions /yúkadpa-rta/ 'husband' (literally 'husband-man'); /mánga-rta/ 'child'; /tíin-ta/ 'this man'; /ngája-rta/ 'which man?, who?'. sweep_summary: Lardil is not in the catalog. The three Glottolog title hits contribute nothing readable: Ito 1986 (UMass dissertation on syllable theory; Lardil appears for apocope/augmentation) is only available as the paywalled Routledge reissue (doi 10.4324/9780429455124), ScholarWorks blocks our network and the author's page lists it without a link; Wilkinson 1988 (LI 19:325-334 squib on Lardil prosodic structure) has no DOI and sits behind JSTOR's bot challenge; Campbell-Kibler 2007 is an American Speech study of English (ING) and accent perception, a Glottolog misattribution. it cites only Klokeid 1976: 29-30 for stress). The best first-hand statement remains Klokeid 1976, section 1.4.6, pp. 29-30, already held by the project: primary word stress on the initial syllable, phrase stress on the last word, with tangka-headed truncated nominals and compounds as phrase-level exceptions. Priorities for acquisition: Wilkinson 1988 medium, Ito 1986 low, Campbell-Kibler none. at updated with a dated addendum.

new_statements.quote: 1.4.6 Stress. Primary word stress is on the initial syllable: /wérne/ 'food'; /thápuji/ 'friend'; /kúthithur/ 'will see'. Primary phrase stress is on the last word of the phrase: /kìin wérne/ 'that food'; /ngìthun thápuji/ 'my friend'; /ngàta niwenthar kúrithur/ 'I'll see him'. There are exceptions to this, namely a set of nominal expressions with /tangka/ 'man' as the head noun, and with a demonstrative of or other modifier preceding the head noun. In these expressions, the noun encliticizes to the modifier, and then undergoes truncation, thus appearing as /-rta/ ... Observe that these nominal expressions have initial, not final, stress. Compounds regularly take final stress: /turlta-wúnta/ 'cloud' (lit. 'excrement-rain').

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word, regardless of length or syllable shape (examples of 2- and 3-syllable words). Within a phrase the last word carries the main phrasal stress; modifier+tangka expressions that have fused into one word (/-rta/) behave as single words with initial stress; compounds stress the final member.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described anywhere in the grammar; the formal rule (p. 175) assigns only [1 stress] to the first vowel of the word and demotes non-final words of a phrase to [2 stress].
new_statements.exceptions: Compounds take stress on the final member (/turlta-wúnta/ 'cloud'); the exceptions listed concern phrase stress (encliticised /tangka/ 'man' expressions such as /yúkarpa-rta/ 'husband', /tíin-ta/ 'this man' keep initial rather than phrase-final stress). No lexical exceptions to word-initial stress are given.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly distinguishes word stress (initial syllable) from phrase stress (last word of phrase) and compound stress (final member); examples are citation forms and short phrases in Klokeid's practical orthography with acute = primary, grave = reduced/phrase-secondary.
new_statements.identity_note: Klokeid 1976 describes Lardil proper (lard1243) as spoken on Mornington Island, based on Hale's 1960/1967 field data and Klokeid's own; it is 'Old Lardil' in Richards' (2001) terms, not the contracted 'New Lardil' of the last speakers, and not the Damin (Demiin) initiation register.
